llm.summary: This planning skill is mostly transparent and non-executable, but it tells the agent to move into an execution phase automatically without asking first.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is implementation planning, but the artifact requires automatic invocation of `Skill(attune:project-execution)` after saving the plan, which can move beyond planning into action-taking behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The workflow is disclosed and has bypass conditions, but it explicitly says not to prompt the user for confirmation before transitioning to execution, reducing user control at a potentially high-impact boundary.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains a single markdown `SKILL.md` file with no executable scripts, hooks, bundled binaries, or install-time commands identified in the artifact metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Writing or checking `docs/implementation-plan.md` is proportionate for a planning skill, but chaining into an execution skill may authorize broader workspace changes than the planning purpose alone implies.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, credential access, background worker, privilege escalation, or hidden local data access is present in the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a planning workflow that can automatically proceed into execution after producing `docs/implementation-plan.md`. To keep tighter control, use `--standalone` or explicitly tell the agent to stop after planning before invoking the skill.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: The auto-continuation instruction is explicitly present. It is related to the Attune workflow, but requiring an execution-phase transition without an affirmative checkpoint is broader than a planning skill needs.
[EA2] unexpected: The `Do NOT prompt the user for confirmation` instruction is present. It is disclosed, not hidden or malicious, but it removes user approval before a potentially side-effecting phase.
